svg.text: GA-28 / GA-29 Dosing leafy and long goods by mass
Don’t count leaves or rods — let the load cell decide: coarse grabs then a trim; rods rolling over a weir.
G-assembly-meat · G9 dosing (recommended)
salad ±15 % → ±8 g achieved
spaghetti ±5 g at 20–40 rods/s
sensing: load cell only
GA-28 Leafy goods: loss-in-weight grabs
a salad tolerates ±15 %: grab, weigh, trim with small tongs
GA-29 Spaghetti: log-roll weir box
rods roll over the box edge one layer at a time
box (or spin basket) on the load cell
salad bowl
target 120 g ±15 % (load cell only)
wide tongs (90 mm): 25–40 g per grab
narrow tongs (30 mm): 5–10 g to trim
last grab > 15 % over → dropped back
error ±8 g on 60–360 g · conf. H
tongs: one bent spring-steel strip each, no hinge
GN 1/3 box, end view: 250 mm rods loaded aligned

g.text: tilted about its long axis just past the friction angle (17–25°)

svg.text: V-tray on the load cell

g.text: target reached → tilt back: the flow stops
V-tray slides the bundle end-first into the pot

svg.text: 1 rod ≈ 1 g · 100–125 g = Ø 24 mm bundle · 20–40 rods/s → ±5 g · conf. M–H
crossed rods at the weir are the risk: a tap clears them; alt.: gauge grab ±10 %
leek, carrot, celery: slice from one piece until the scale says stop

g.text: 1/4 Leafy goods: wide tongs take 25–40 g per grab from the box on the load cell.
2/4 When less than a grab is missing, narrow tongs trim with 5–10 g — the scale is the only sensor.
3/4 Spaghetti: tilting the box past the friction angle lets the rods roll out one layer at a time; tilting back stops them.
4/4 The V-tray on the scale holds the weighed bundle and slides it end-first into the pot.
